t: This is the site of The Clink, a prison in Southwark that operated from the twelfth century until 1780. It stood beside Winchester Palace, the London residence of the Bishop of Winchester, who owned this local manor, the Liberty of the Clink. He kept its revenues, and could jail people who failed to pay, as well as heretics. It was possibly the oldest men's prison and probably the oldest women's prison in England. George Blackwell, Roman Catholic Archpriest of England from 1597 to 1608, died here in 1613.
